summary: Postback dedupe fingerprint collision caused duplicate hourly charge and provisional overage on finalized invoice
description: Issue summary: Customer noticed a one-off provisional overage line and a negative adjustment on their finalized invoice for the billing window 2026-03-07 00:00 to 2026-03-08 00:00. The invoice shows an extra ~1.2M token charge (~€1,430) that Atlas claims does not match their internal job reports. Impact: Customer-facing finance alert with escalations to their procurement team; potential churn risk if not resolved within SLA. Environment: Dedicated account in eu-west using reserved pool; scheduled batch embedding jobs from Atlas across midnight UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer ran scheduled batch (daily embeddings) at 23:50 UTC on 2026-03-07. 2) Batch completed successfully; customer-side logs show single submission. 3) At 00:30 UTC, billing pipeline ingested two postbacks with identical job IDs but different arrival fingerprints. Observed logs: Postback-reconciler logs show duplicate postback ingestion with distinct fingerprint values despite identical origin headers. Dedupe-cache traces show TTL hit and a cache eviction event at 00:28 UTC for the same job key. Hypothesis: A fingerprint collision combined with a short-lived TTL bug in the dedupe cache caused the reconciler to treat a replayed postback as a fresh event for the hourly accumulator. The late-arriving replay then passed through the aggregator when the original fingerprint entry had been evicted, resulting in double-counting in the hourly accumulator and a provisional overage line. Timeline: 2026-03-07 23:50 Customer submits batch. 2026-03-08 00:01 First postback ingested. 2026-03-08 00:28 Dedupe cache eviction recorded. 2026-03-08 00:30 Second (replay) postback ingested with different fingerprint and counted again. Investigation observed: - Dedupe key generation code uses CRC32 + truncated salt (legacy). Collision probability increased for larger batches. - Cache TTL configured to 30 minutes for dedupe entries; under memory pressure for eu-west it was evicting earlier than TTL (observed eviction spikes). - Aggregator does not cross-check job_id uniqueness when fingerprint differs. Next steps listed below.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 Customer (Atlas HealthTech): We received an unexpected overage line on our March invoice — looks like the daily embed job was charged twice. Our internal job ID shows only one run. Can you confirm?
2026-03-10 09:27 Support (Asha Patel): Thanks for reporting — opened SUP-100111 and have escalated to billing and infra. Can you attach job IDs and raw postback payloads?

2026-03-10 10:05 Customer: Attached job_id=atlas-embed-20260307-2350 and two postback payloads exported from our side. Only one outgoing webhook was sent. We also see one success webhook from provider side.

2026-03-10 11:40 Eng (Miguel Torres): Initial triage: found two postback events in reconciler with same job_id but different "fingerprint" values. Found dedupe-cache eviction spike at 00:28 UTC. Suspect fingerprint collision + early eviction. Adding billing engineer.

2026-03-10 12:10 Billing (Leah Chen): We will freeze provisional invoice adjustments until investigation completes. If double-counting confirmed, we'll apply a corrective credit to the next cycle or issue a one-off refund per customer preference.

2026-03-11 15:22 Eng (Miguel Torres): Reproduced local collision with synthetic workload using CRC32 truncation. Created patch candidate to switch to SHA256-derived fingerprint and extend dedupe TTL to 24h for job-level entries. Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/452

2026-03-12 08:34 Support (Asha Patel): Shared interim status with customer — confirmed we are not charging while billing holds adjustments. Customer requested timeline for final credit (prefers immediate invoice credit).
investigation_notes: Confirmed two reconciler events with identical job_id and payload checksum but different dedupe fingerprints.
Reproducer: synthetic 10k-job run produced fingerprint collision in 1/120k runs using CRC32 truncation; switching to SHA256 removes collisions in reproduced tests.
Memory pressure in eu-west cluster correlated with pod restarts in the dedupe-cache deployment at 00:27-00:29 UTC — eviction triggered earlier than configured TTL.
Aggregator change required: prefer job_id-level idempotency check in addition to fingerprint to prevent double-counting when fingerprints mismatch.
Billing provisional hold placed per Leah; pending final credit decision after patch rollout and backfill run.
Suggested mitigation: backfill hourly accumulator with deduped postbacks for 2026-03-07 window, apply credit equal to duplicated token count (estimated 1,214,786 tokens).
workaround: Billing has placed a provisional hold on the overage. For production prevention, advise customers to add a short delay (30s) between job submission and expected postback arrival for critical batches while we deploy the server-side patch.
